title: The Battle of Tours
description: October 732. Charles Martel's Frankish infantry must hold the wooded high ground between Tours and Poitiers against the Umayyad cavalry of Abd al-Rahman. A third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo can be rallied to strike the enemy camp. Victory requires repelling the cavalry charges and forcing the invaders' withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR stands in for Charles Martel - a Norman duke of 1066, over three centuries after Tours, and the engine offers other Frankish/generic hero options
SALADIN represents Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi - a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan, wrong dynasty, wrong region (Egypt/Syria) and wrong century for an 8th-century Umayyad governor of al-Andalus
EL_CID represents Duke Odo of Aquitaine - an 11th-century Castilian, and El Cid's Spanish-Christian identity actively confuses the Aquitanian role
14 CAMEL_RIDER in the Umayyad army: the force that crossed the Pyrenees fought as Arab-Berber horse; camels were not a battlefield arm in Gaul

The Umayyad camp is a stone CASTLE with 60 STONE_WALL segments and 4 GUARD_TOWERS - the historical raiders had a wagon-and-plunder field camp, not masonry fortification, and the victory text calls it a 'stronghold'
PAVILION_A / TENT_A for Odo's Aquitanians gives a Middle-Eastern nomad camp look to a Gallo-Roman Christian duchy
